_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Remove `Cs` from the generated XPath `CATEGORIES` table.**

`category_spans()` returns every two-letter General_Category value in `UnicodeData.txt`, and that includes `Cs`. `xpath()` emits every entry as a named category. `Parser::property` in `crates/rdf-core/src/xsd_regex/xpath/compile.rs` accepts any name that the table contains. As a result, the native compiler accepts `\p{Cs}` and `\P{Cs}`.

XML Schema Part 2 Appendix G defines a closed `IsCategory` list. That list has `C`, `Cc`, `Cf`, `Co` and `Cn`, but not `Cs`. The compatibility compiler follows that list: `IS_CATEGORY_NAMES` in `crates/rdf-core/src/xsd_regex/emit.rs` has no `Cs`, so `\p{Cs}` fails there with `UnknownCategory`. The native profiles therefore accept a pattern that both dated grammars reject. PR objective `#406` requires profile-specific grammar vectors, and this case violates them.

Remove `Cs` after the one-letter groups are built. The `C` group can keep its surrogate ranges. Those ranges have no effect, because a `&str` cannot contain surrogates. Add `\p{Cs}` to the rejected list in the compiler tests.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
     for kind in ["L", "M", "N", "P", "Z", "S", "C"] {
         let spans = merge(
             categories
                 .iter()
                 .filter(|(name, _)| name.len() == 2 && name.starts_with(kind))
                 .flat_map(|(_, spans)| spans.iter().copied()),
         );
         categories.insert(kind.to_owned(), spans);
     }
+    // Appendix G's closed IsCategory list has no `Cs`.
+    categories.remove("Cs");
```
</details>

```suggestion
fn xpath() -> String {
    let mut categories = category_spans();
    for kind in ["L", "M", "N", "P", "Z", "S", "C"] {
        let spans = merge(
            categories
                .iter()
                .filter(|(name, _)| name.len() == 2 && name.starts_with(kind))
                .flat_map(|(_, spans)| spans.iter().copied()),
        );
        categories.insert(kind.to_owned(), spans);
    }
    // Appendix G's closed IsCategory list has no `Cs`.
    categories.remove("Cs");
```

</details>

**Do not retain non-operational query diagnostics across tolerated failures.**

`crates/shapes/src/sparql.rs` maps query failures to `xpath::query_error`, which captures the first cause. `SomeValue` can discard an inner failure when a later value conforms. `root_result` then promotes the pending cause and can fail the otherwise conforming focus with `XPathValidationError::Query`.

Capture only operational query refusals at `query_error`. If cleanup occurs at tolerant constraint sites, clear only non-operational query causes. Keep native pattern resource and allocation refusals fatal.

Do not classify these query diagnostics with `xpath::Resource` codes. Those codes belong to native XPath errors. SPARQL diagnostics use their own `native-sparql-*` codes.
